title: Entanglement in the ring — 32 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit and how they are bound
description:
Entanglement in the ring — 32 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the ring. 32 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 10 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 94 pair(s); the theorems fall into 6 strand(s), the largest of 17. Most binding: m9 (8), R (7), pw (6), closure (5), refl (4), orbit6 (4).

2 · Imports. Built on: reversal.lean. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 2 file(s): src/proof/z9plus.lean, src/proof/reversal.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 32 sealed receipts fold to c33aca9a-7c2b-8fb6-856f-d6d5edf66b39. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (0, 6, 1, 3, 4, 8, 6). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: coin.lean (6 observed, 4.26 expected, lift 1.41), demand.lean (4 observed, 2.84 expected, lift 1.41), families.lean (21 observed, 14.91 expected, lift 1.41). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 15.46; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.45. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 100.0% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. digital roots (casting out nines) — in use by the 12th century; the Pisano period — after Leonardo Pisano; studied by Joseph-Louis Lagrange, 1774 Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.

The theorems.

  1. squares_land_exactly_in_zero_one_four_seven — R.all (fun d => [0, 1, 4, 7].contains (m9 (d * d))) ∧ [0, 1, 4, 7].all (fun s => R.any (fun d => m9 (d * d) == s)) record
  2. five_is_not_a_square_mod_nine — ¬ (R.any (fun d => m9 (d * d) == 5)) record
  3. cubes_land_exactly_in_zero_one_eight — R.all (fun d => [0, 1, 8].contains (pw d 3)) ∧ [0, 1, 8].all (fun c => R.any (fun d => pw d 3 == c)) record
  4. primitive_roots_are_exactly_two_and_five — (R.filter generates) = [2, 5] record
  5. primitive_root_iff_generates_the_units — R.all (fun g => generates g == ([2, 5].contains g)) record
  6. doubling_has_period_six — (List.range 30).all (fun k => pw 2 k == pw 2 (k + 6)) record
  7. no_period_smaller_than_six — ¬ ([1, 2, 3, 4, 5].any (fun p => (List.range 12).all (fun k => pw 2 k == pw 2 (k + p)))) record
  8. digital_root_agrees_with_the_residue — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => (dr n == 9) == (m9 n == 0)) record
  9. digital_root_is_the_digit_sum_residue — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => m9 (digitSum n) == m9 n) record
  10. reversal_cannot_change_the_digital_root — (List.range' 1 300).all (fun n => dr (reverseNum n) == dr n) record
  11. orbit_digital_roots_have_period_six — (List.range 24).all (fun k => dr (pw 2 k) == dr (pw 2 (k + 6))) record
  12. the_orders_of_the_units_are_exact — ord 1 = 1 ∧ ord 8 = 2 ∧ ord 4 = 3 ∧ ord 7 = 3 ∧ ord 2 = 6 ∧ ord 5 = 6 record
  13. the_unit_table_is_a_latin_square — [1,2,4,5,7,8].all (fun a => (([1,2,4,5,7,8].map (fun b => m9 (a * b))).eraseDups).length == 6 ∧ [1,2,4,5,7,8].all (fun c => [1,2,4,5,7,8].any (fun b => m9 (a * b) == c))) record
  14. the_orbit_never_meets_the_triad — (List.range 40).all (fun k => ! [0, 3, 6].contains (pw 2 k)) record
  15. the_reflected_orbit_covers_the_whole_triad — [3, 6, 9].all (fun t => orbit6.any (fun d => refl d == t)) record
  16. reflection_splits_the_orbit_in_half — (orbit6.filter (fun d => [3, 6, 9].contains (refl d))).length = 3 ∧ (orbit6.filter (fun d => ! [3, 6, 9].contains (refl d))).length = 3 record
  17. the_crossing_pairs_are_one_four_seven — (orbit6.filter (fun d => [3, 6, 9].contains (refl d))) = [1, 4, 7] ∧ refl 1 = 9 ∧ refl 4 = 6 ∧ refl 7 = 3 record
  18. reflection_is_injective_on_the_orbit — ((orbit6.map refl).eraseDups).length = 6 record
  19. doubling_alone_reaches_only_the_units — ((List.range 12).map (fun k => pw 2 k)).eraseDups.length = 6 ∧ ((List.range 12).map (fun k => pw 2 k)).all (fun d => ! [0, 3, 6].contains d) record
  20. reflection_alone_reaches_only_two — (closure 6 [1]).length ≥ 2 ∧ rfl9 1 = 0 ∧ rfl9 (rfl9 1) = 1 record
  21. doubling_and_reflection_together_reach_every_residue — (closure 4 [1]).length = 9 record
  22. every_residue_is_reachable_from_one — (List.range 9).all (fun d => (closure 4 [1]).contains d) record
  23. the_diameter_is_exactly_four — (closure 4 [1]).length = 9 ∧ (closure 3 [1]).length = 7 record
  24. the_frontier_grows_by_two_each_round — (closure 0 [1]).length = 1 ∧ (closure 1 [1]).length = 3 ∧ (closure 2 [1]).length = 5 ∧ (closure 3 [1]).length = 7 ∧ (closure 4 [1]).length = 9 record
  25. product_of_the_units_is_minus_one — m9 ([1,2,4,5,7,8].foldl (· * ·) 1) = 8 ∧ m9 (8 + 1) = 0 record
  26. pisano_period_mod_nine_is_twenty_four — (List.range 30).all (fun k => fib9 k == fib9 (k + 24)) record
  27. no_proper_divisor_of_twenty_four_is_a_period — ¬ ([1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12].any (fun p => (List.range 26).all (fun k => fib9 k == fib9 (k + p)))) record
  28. fibonacci_recurrence_holds — (List.range 20).all (fun n => fib (n + 2) == fib n + fib (n + 1)) record
  29. consecutive_fibonacci_are_coprime — (List.range' 1 25).all (fun n => gcd9 (fib n) (fib (n + 1)) == 1) record
  30. three_five_eight_are_consecutive_fibonacci — fib 4 = 3 ∧ fib 5 = 5 ∧ fib 6 = 8 ∧ fib 4 + fib 5 = fib 6 record
  31. units_and_triad_partition_the_ring — ((R.filter (fun d => R.any (fun e => m9 (d * e) == 1))).length + (R.filter (fun d => ! R.any (fun e => m9 (d * e) == 1))).length) = 9 record
  32. both_parts_sum_to_zero — m9 ((R.filter (fun d => R.any (fun e => m9 (d * e) == 1))).foldl (· + ·) 0) == 0 ∧ m9 ((R.filter (fun d => ! R.any (fun e => m9 (d * e) == 1))).foldl (· + ·) 0) == 0 record
